commons-contents-check.desc: Verifies that the files in each commons module (see import-rules check) only specify the following top-level items as public (i.e. any other top-level public items are a violation): - `t` - `struct`, `enum`, `type` alias, and `trait` - `s` - `static` - `cnst` - `const` - `ext_traits` - `trait` - `c` - `fn`
commons-contents-check.note: The nearest enclosing commons module decides which rule applies (e.g. a file in `s/c/` is judged as `c`).
commons-contents-check.rationale: The commons-items check is one-directional: it says a public type must live in `t`, but not that `t` may hold only public types. Since commons-exports mandates a glob re-export, the public surface of `t` is whatever its submodules make public, so a stray `pub fn` in a `t` submodule becomes `t::name()` - a call qualified by a module name that carries no meaning, which is what call-rules exists to prevent. This check is the converse of the location checks, and the pair makes the flattened `use ...::t::TypeName` import safe.
commons-contents-check.exemption: Items restricted to a visibility that cannot escape the commons module (i.e. `pub(super)`)
